name: Channels
description: Where people reach the agent. Messaging-native agents live in the apps people already use.

name: Interface
description: How results are shown. From plain text to generative UI and canvases the agent draws itself.

name: Voice
description: Speech in, speech out, or full-duplex realtime conversation.

name: Devices
description: Hardware and nodes the agent can see, hear or act through.

name: Model
description: The reasoning core. Frontier closed models, open weights, or a mix routed per task.

name: Router
description: One API in front of many models: fallbacks, cost and latency routing, keys.

name: Inference host
description: Who actually runs open-weight models, when you're not using a lab's own API.

name: Harness
description: The agent loop: prompt, call tools, observe, repeat. Owns context, compaction and sessions.

name: Persona
description: Instruction files that shape who the agent is and how it works in a project.

name: Multi-agent
description: Delegation: subagents, handoffs, swarms, and agents talking to other people's agents.

name: Core tools
description: Built-in actions the loop can take. Coding agents start from read, write, edit, bash.

name: Protocols
description: Open standards that let agents plug into tools, editors and each other.

name: Connectors
description: Authenticated access to the user's SaaS: Gmail, GitHub, Notion, Salesforce…

name: Skills
description: Procedural knowledge loaded on demand: folders of instructions, scripts and resources.

name: Compute
description: Where the agent's code runs. Rauch: 'EC2 becomes compute for code written by agents.'

name: Browser use
description: Seeing and driving websites and desktops when there's no API.

name: Memory
description: What the agent remembers across sessions about you and its work. Usually several at once: files, a user model, a graph, an API.

name: Retrieval
description: Search over documents and history: vectors, keywords, rerankers.

name: State
description: Where sessions, transcripts and files live. Rauch's 'files' leg of brain, hands, files.

name: Proactivity
description: What wakes the agent up when nobody's talking to it.

name: Durable execution
description: Long-running work that survives crashes, waits for humans, and resumes.

name: Guardrails
description: Who may do what. Graded autonomy, pre-action review, injection defense.

name: Identity & secrets
description: Credentials the model never sees, and an identity for the agent itself.

name: Payments
description: Letting agents buy things, and get paid, safely.

name: Observability
description: Traces, evals and costs, so you know what the agent actually did.

name: Hosting
description: Where the agent itself lives and runs.

name: Agent readiness
description: Making your own site and APIs usable by other people's agents.
